No, you're one version behind. The installed `ac` is 0.8.20, and production is serving 0.8.21.

0.8.21 is commit d76b25f4f6 ("Preview animated SVGs on the Aesel card"). It's on origin/main but this checkout hasn't pulled it. Local HEAD here is still at 0.8.19, with an uncommitted bump to 0.8.20 in `aesel/package.json`.

Running Aesel's update will get you 0.8.21. Before pulling, sort out the uncommitted bump in this checkout, because it will conflict with the version line on origin.

Not as things are set up. Your `ac` isn't an installed release. `~/.local/bin/ac` is a symlink into this repo, at `aesel/bin/easel`, so you're running whatever the working copy holds.

The update check in `aesel/src/updates.mjs:119` skips that case on purpose. It only runs when `install.json` is present, and that file only exists in a packed release tarball. A checkout gets no check at all, so the code can never overwrite source you're editing. That's why no `.update-check.json` exists here and it never phoned home.

So for you, getting the latest means `git pull`, and Aesel stays quiet about it. That's arguably a gap. A checkout could still notice when the served `aesel.json` is newer than its own `package.json` and say "origin has 0.8.21, pull", without installing anything. That would have caught this. I can add it if you want.

Yes, it's fixed in the source now. Your `ac` won't show the change until it restarts.

The reason it stayed quiet: when Aesel runs from a checkout, the launch check only looked at your own `aesel/package.json`. If that file moved past the version the window started with, it showed the banner. It never asked the site what the latest version was. You hadn't pulled, so as far as it could tell nothing had changed.

Now a checkout also fetches `aesel.json` at launch and every half hour after, in `aesel/src/tui.mjs` around line 3398. If the site serves a newer version than your files, the banner says "Aesel 0.8.21 is out · this checkout is behind · git pull, then /update". In that state `/update` tells you to pull rather than restarting into the same code. Once you pull, the same banner turns into the usual "ready" one, and `/update` restarts you into the new code. It still never installs anything into a checkout, and if the fetch fails it says nothing. The banner text is in `aesel/src/render.mjs:1047`, and I added a render test for it.

Tests: 550 pass and 1 fails. The failure is "visible history matches a full layout…" in `test/tui-performance.test.mjs`. That test doesn't involve updates, and the file already had uncommitted changes before I started, as did `render.mjs` and `tui.mjs`. I didn't check whether it also fails without my edits, though. For the same reason I haven't committed: my changes sit in the same files as that other uncommitted work. Do you want me to commit just my hunks, or wait until that work lands?
